discoveries.mechanism: Dealers intermediate an unconditional client demand for USD at the fixes; USD appreciates into the fix and depreciates after it as dealer inventory is unwound (W-shaped USD path). Post-London-fix window is 11:00-17:00 ET (16:00-22:00 London): foreign currency up vs USD. Broker stamps assume the venue clock UTC+3 summer / UTC+2 winter (CLAUDE.md); stamp 18 opens at 16:00 London in both seasons.
discoveries.firm: Krohn, Mueller, Whelan (Bank of Canada / Warwick / CBS)
discoveries.source_title: Foreign Exchange Fixings and Returns around the Clock
discoveries.quote: The U.S. dollar appreciates in the run-up to foreign exchange fixes and depreciates thereafter, tracing a W-shaped return pattern around the clock.
discoveries.reported_effect: Dollar portfolio +1.84bp (t=5.48) post-London fix 1999-2019, G9 pairs; paper finds client-market cost-adjusted returns significantly NEGATIVE, liquidity-provision returns positive
discoveries.cost_caveat: Test at the desk's measured raw-spread + commission; the paper's client costs kill it, so it lives only if Fusion raw-spread costs are below ~1bp round trip or entries are passive limits.

discoveries.mechanism: Mirror of the post-London-fix USD depreciation for USD-base pairs (USD falls after the fix => USDXXX down). Broker stamps assume the venue clock UTC+3 summer / UTC+2 winter (CLAUDE.md); stamp 18 opens at 16:00 London in both seasons.
discoveries.source_title: Foreign Exchange Fixings and Returns around the Clock
discoveries.quote: the U.S. dollar gradually appreciates against all currencies ahead of the three major currency fixes in Tokyo, Frankfurt (the ECB fix) and London
discoveries.reported_effect: same W-pattern; yen is the exception after London (depreciates post-London fix) - exclude USDJPY from this cell

discoveries.mechanism: Pre-ECB-fix leg of the W: USD appreciates 02:00-08:15 ET (07:00-13:15 London) into the 14:15 CET ECB fix. Approximated with the london_open catalogue moment (07:00 London = stamp 10 summer) held 6 bars; an exact ecb_fix label is a capability gap below.
discoveries.source_title: Foreign Exchange Fixings and Returns around the Clock
discoveries.reported_effect: Dollar portfolio -1.68bp (USD up, t=-4.51) in the pre-ECB window 1999-2019

discoveries.mechanism: Tokyo 9:55 fix: Japanese importers' predictable USD buying at the fixing (especially gotobi days 5,10,15,20,25,30 and month-end) lifts USDJPY into the fix; USD reverts after (post-Tokyo window). tokyo_open (00:00 UTC) sits 55 min before the 9:55 JST fix; exact tokyo_fix label is a gap.
discoveries.source_title: Puzzles in the Forex Tokyo 'Fixing': Order Imbalances and Biased Pricing by Banks
discoveries.quote: The customer orders are biased toward buying the foreign currencies, which is predictable.
discoveries.reported_effect: Krohn: dollar portfolio -1.99bp pre-Tokyo, +2.10bp post-Tokyo (1999-2019); a yen strategy around the Tokyo fix grew $1 to $12.2 gross
discoveries.conditioning: gotobi days and month-end strengthen the effect (Ito-Yamada)

discoveries.mechanism: Post-Tokyo-fix unwind: USD (and crosses bought vs JPY for settlement) give back the fix premium after 9:55 JST.
discoveries.source_title: Foreign Exchange Fixings and Returns around the Clock
discoveries.reported_effect: post-Tokyo window 20:55-02:00 ET, dollar portfolio +2.10bp (t=9.19)

discoveries.mechanism: Abnormal price moves into the 4pm WMR fix revert after it: fix orders add volatility and negative serial correlation around the fix across 18 of 21 currencies. Complements Krohn: here the signal is the size of the pre-fix displacement, not the unconditional USD path.
discoveries.source_title: Forex Trading and the WMR Fix
discoveries.quote: forex price changes display extraordinary volatility and negative serial correlation around the Fix.
discoveries.reported_effect: significant negative serial correlation in 18 currencies; 'large enough to support trading strategies ... that appeared economically attractive at the time' (pre-2015 reform)

discoveries.mechanism: Local currencies depreciate during their own trading hours and appreciate outside them because local participants are net buyers of foreign currency in their own hours (order-flow corroborated). EUR/GBP weaken in European hours.
discoveries.source_title: Intraday Patterns in FX Returns and Order Flow
discoveries.quote: a significant tendency for currencies to depreciate during local trading hours.
discoveries.reported_effect: EUR/USD simple open-to-close strategy profitable after costs in 1997-2007 EBS data; hourly annualised log-return effects significant at 1%

discoveries.mechanism: US-hours leg of the local-hours depreciation: USD weakens in US trading hours (foreign currency rises), as also found by Cornett et al. (1995) on IMM futures cited inside Breedon-Ranaldo.
discoveries.source_title: Intraday Patterns in FX Returns and Order Flow
discoveries.quote: local currencies tend to depreciate during their own trading hours and appreciate outside them
discoveries.reported_effect: EUR/USD USD-session coefficient significant (JMCB 2013 Table 2)

discoveries.mechanism: AUD depreciates in its own (Asian) hours: AUDUSD down during the Sydney/Tokyo session (paper: AUD-session coefficient negative, USD-session positive).
discoveries.source_title: Intraday Patterns in FX Returns and Order Flow
discoveries.reported_effect: AUD/USD AUD-session annualised coefficient -0.028 (1%), USD-session +0.016 (1%)

discoveries.mechanism: JPY depreciates in its own (Tokyo) hours: USDJPY up during the Tokyo session.
discoveries.source_title: Intraday Patterns in FX Returns and Order Flow
discoveries.reported_effect: USD/JPY mixed on EBS quotes, significant on customer order flow

discoveries.mechanism: Safe-haven currencies (CHF, JPY) appreciate when US equities fall and FX vol rises, over horizons from hours to days; a lagged version tests whether the haven bid continues after an equity down-bar (USDJPY/USDCHF fall after US500 falls).
discoveries.source_title: Safe Haven Currencies
discoveries.reported_effect: safe-haven properties at granularities from a few hours to several days, ordinary days and crises, non-linear (stronger in stress)

discoveries.mechanism: Cross-sectional currency momentum: sort currencies (vs USD) on past 1-month excess return into sextiles; long top, short bottom, hold 1 month. Under/over-reaction; distinct from carry; profits concentrated in hard-to-trade currencies (limits to arbitrage).
discoveries.source_title: Currency momentum strategies
discoveries.quote: We find a significant cross-sectional spread in excess returns of up to 10% per annum (p.a.) between past winner and loser currencies.
discoveries.reported_effect: 6-10% p.a. for 1-month holding (1976-2010); fades monotonically with longer holding; partially explained by transaction costs

discoveries.mechanism: Currency value: currencies that appreciated most over the past 5 years (strong real exchange rate) earn low subsequent excess returns; buy 5-year losers, sell 5-year winners. Better if RER is purged of productivity, NFA, export quality, output gap (capability gap).
discoveries.source_title: Currency Value
discoveries.quote: going long countries with high 5-year appreciation rates forecasts low excess returns relative to currencies which depreciated over the last 5 years.
discoveries.reported_effect: simple RER value Sharpe ~0.5 p.a.; fundamentals-adjusted 0.8-0.9 p.a.; distinct from carry and momentum

discoveries.mechanism: HML-FX carry: long high-interest-rate currencies, short low-rate funders; high-rate currencies load more on a global slope/risk factor. On CFDs carry is the broker swap differential (swap_diff).
discoveries.source_title: Common Risk Factors in Currency Markets
discoveries.reported_effect: HML-FX slope factor explains most cross-sectional variation between high and low interest-rate currency portfolios

discoveries.mechanism: Carry pays a premium for global FX-volatility risk: high-yielders fall when global FX vol spikes; low-yielders hedge. Holding carry only in calm/declining vol (or scaling by inverse variance, Moreira-Muir) harvests the premium while sidestepping the crash state.
discoveries.firm: Menkhoff et al.; Moreira & Muir; Brunnermeier, Nagel, Pedersen
discoveries.source_title: Carry Trades and Global Foreign Exchange Volatility
discoveries.reported_effect: global FX vol innovations explain >90% of the spread across 5 carry portfolios; vol-managed carry raises Sharpe (Moreira-Muir document it for the carry trade)

discoveries.mechanism: Carry crash dynamics: negative skew from sudden unwinding when funding liquidity falls; 'carry-trade losses reduce future crash risk but increase the price of crash risk' -> re-entry after a carry drawdown earns a higher premium.
discoveries.source_title: Carry Trades and Currency Crashes
discoveries.reported_effect: documented negative skew and liquidity link; the re-entry trade itself is SPECULATED

discoveries.mechanism: Carry generalised to every asset: expected return = carry (model-free, known ex ante) + expected price change. For CFDs the broker's daily swap long/short encodes the futures basis / dividend-minus-rate / roll, so 'carry' is directly observable on every instrument.
discoveries.source_title: Carry
discoveries.quote: carry predicts returns both in the cross section and time series for a variety of different asset classes
discoveries.reported_effect: carry strategies profitable across equities, bonds, commodities, currencies, Treasuries, credit, options; crash together in global recessions

discoveries.mechanism: Value and momentum everywhere: 12-1 month momentum across commodities (and in every asset class), negatively correlated with value; combine both. Commodity cross-section is the cleanest CFD analogue.
discoveries.source_title: Value and Momentum Everywhere
discoveries.reported_effect: value and momentum premia in every asset class; value-momentum negatively correlated within and across classes

discoveries.mechanism: Commodity-currency exchange rates are forward-looking asset prices that embed expected commodity prices, so AUD/NZD/CAD/ZAR moves lead commodity price indices out of sample (not vice versa).
discoveries.source_title: Can Exchange Rates Forecast Commodity Prices?
discoveries.reported_effect: robust in-sample and out-of-sample predictive power for global commodity prices, quarterly data 1-3 decades

discoveries.mechanism: Oil prices and the Canadian dollar are linked at the daily frequency (oil ~21% of Canadian exports); lagged oil shocks predict USDCAD but only ephemerally, after allowing for instability.
discoveries.source_title: Can Oil Prices Forecast Exchange Rates?
discoveries.quote: the predictive ability is ephemeral, mostly appearing after instabilities have been appropriately taken into account
discoveries.reported_effect: stable contemporaneous daily link; lagged predictability weak/time-varying - treat as a regime-gated lead_lag

discoveries.mechanism: News diffuses from the US with a lag: lagged US returns predict non-US index returns, not vice versa (information frictions). On D1 the Asian open after a US close is the tradable lag.
discoveries.source_title: International Stock Return Predictability: What Is the Role of the United States?
discoveries.horizon: monthly in paper; test D1 and next-session
discoveries.reported_effect: lagged US returns significantly predict returns in numerous non-US industrialized countries

discoveries.mechanism: Short-term changes in speculators' (non-commercial) net positions are liquidity demands; commercials supply that liquidity and are paid for it, so futures returns move against recent speculator position changes.
discoveries.source_title: A Tale of Two Premiums: The Role of Hedgers and Speculators in Commodity Futures Markets
discoveries.reported_effect: liquidity-provision gains of commercials largely offset the hedging premium they pay (JF 2020)

discoveries.mechanism: Hedging-pressure premium: long commodities where hedgers are net short and speculators net long, short where hedgers are net long; premium rises with market volatility.
discoveries.source_title: Capturing the risk premium of commodity futures: The role of hedging pressure
discoveries.reported_effect: positive, significant long-short premia with Sharpe ratios exceeding long-only commodity portfolios

discoveries.mechanism: FALSIFIER PRIOR: speculator net-position changes coincide with FX moves in the SAME week (75% directional hit) but carry no information for the following week. Expect cot_change_momentum on FX to fail once the Friday publication lag is respected (the desk's _cot_entries already enters the Monday after).
discoveries.source_title: Exchange Rate Changes and Net Positions of Speculators in the Futures Market
discoveries.quote: net positions do not appear to be useful for anticipating exchange rate moves over the following week.
discoveries.reported_effect: contemporaneous 75% direction accuracy; ~no next-week predictability (6 currencies, 10 years)

discoveries.mechanism: Index funds (GSCI) roll front to next contract on the 5th-9th business day; front-runners and the roll itself depress the front/next spread, which reverts afterwards. CFD transfer is SPECULATED: CFDs roll with the underlying, so the outright effect is diluted.
discoveries.source_title: Limits to Arbitrage and Commodity Index Investment: Front-Running the Goldman Roll
discoveries.reported_effect: front-running spread strategies Sharpe up to 4.39, 2000-Mar 2010 (spread, not outright)

discoveries.mechanism: EIA weekly petroleum inventory surprises have an immediate inverse price impact; EIA-day returns predict subsequent intraday returns (informed traders arrive, liquidity thins), i.e., post-release drift.
discoveries.firm: Wen, Indriawan, Lien, Xu; Halova, Kurov, Kucher
discoveries.source_title: Intraday Return Predictability in the Crude Oil Market: The Role of EIA Inventory Announcements
discoveries.reported_effect: EIA announcement days contribute to crude intraday momentum (Energy Journal 2023)

discoveries.mechanism: Natural-gas weekly storage report (Thu 10:30 ET): surprise vs expectations moves price; the Halova-Kurov-Kucher correction for noisy expectations strengthens the measured impact.
discoveries.source_title: Noisy Inventory Announcements and Energy Prices
discoveries.reported_effect: inventory surprises significantly move energy prices once measurement error in expectations is addressed

discoveries.mechanism: Gold autumn effect: September and November are the only months with significantly positive gold returns (hedging demand ahead of the equity 'Halloween' season, Indian wedding-season jewellery demand).
discoveries.source_title: The autumn effect of gold

discoveries.mechanism: Second leg of the gold autumn effect (November).
discoveries.source_title: The autumn effect of gold

discoveries.mechanism: Benchmark-fixing leakage in gold: volume and volatility jump at the start of the London PM fix, and early-fix trades predict the fix direction (>90% in some cases) with no effect after publication; the tradable remnant is the pre-benchmark push and its fade. Mapped to the nearest catalogue moment (COMEX settle); the LBMA 15:00 London auction needs its own label (gap).
discoveries.source_title: Fixing a Leaky Fixing: Short-Term Market Reactions to the London PM Gold Price Fixing
discoveries.reported_effect: significant return advantages in the 4 minutes after fix start (pre-2015 fixing; post-2015 LBMA auction may differ)

discoveries.mechanism: Gold/platinum Tokyo day session is dominated by liquidity (uninformed) trading while New York hours carry informed trading; Asian-session displacement should revert in London/NY while NY-session moves persist. SPECULATED trading translation of a microstructure finding.
discoveries.source_title: Intraday seasonality in efficiency, liquidity, volatility and volume: Platinum and gold futures in Tokyo and New York
discoveries.reported_effect: liquidity trading prevalent in Tokyo day session, informed trading in NY day session

discoveries.mechanism: Market intraday momentum: return from prior close to the last half-hour predicts the last half-hour, because option market makers and leveraged ETFs hedging short gamma must trade with the move into the close; stronger on volatile, high-volume and macro-news days, reverting over following days.
discoveries.firm: Gao, Han, Li, Zhou; Baltussen, Da, Lammers, Martens (Robeco)
discoveries.source_title: Hedging demand and market intraday momentum
discoveries.quote: Hedging short gamma exposure requires trading in the direction of price movements, thereby creating price momentum.
discoveries.horizon: last 30-60 min of the cash session
discoveries.reported_effect: Gao: predictive R2 1.6% (2.6% with the 12th half-hour), SPY 1993-2013; Baltussen: 60+ futures 1974-2020, momentum everywhere
discoveries.note: close_hour 22 = broker stamp of the last cash hour (15:00-16:00 ET) under UTC+3/+2 summer/winter alignment of US DST; verify per season

discoveries.mechanism: Same gamma-hedging intraday momentum documented for bond, commodity and currency futures; each instrument's own settlement close must be used (UST 15:00 ET, COMEX gold 13:30 ET, NYMEX crude 14:30 ET, CME FX 14:00 ET).
discoveries.source_title: Hedging demand and market intraday momentum
discoveries.quote: we find strong market intraday momentum everywhere
discoveries.horizon: last 30 min before each venue close
discoveries.reported_effect: timing strategies with very high Sharpe ratios and >0.5 daily success rates across asset classes (Table 6); rest-of-day signal beats overnight in all classes but currencies

discoveries.mechanism: FX intraday momentum on MICEX RUB: first half-hour predicts last half-hour, attributed to liquidity providers' aversion to overnight inventory (not informed trading).
discoveries.source_title: Intraday momentum in FX markets: Disentangling informed trading from liquidity provision
discoveries.reported_effect: significant positive first-to-last half-hour relation 2005-2014 (tick data)
discoveries.tradability: EURRUB/USDRUB CFD liquidity and sanctions-era pricing make this low priority

discoveries.mechanism: S&P 500 futures earn their entire average return in the four hours around the European open, as European investors process overnight information and uncertainty (VIX futures) resolves; the other 20 hours average a noisy zero.
discoveries.source_title: Market Return Around the Clock: A Puzzle
discoveries.reported_effect: Sharpe 1.6, positive every year 2006-2018, survives costs (E-mini)

discoveries.mechanism: Second half of the European-open window (see previous row).
discoveries.source_title: Market Return Around the Clock: A Puzzle
discoveries.reported_effect: same

discoveries.mechanism: Tug of war between overnight and intraday clienteles: momentum profits accrue overnight, reversal-type profits intraday; the index-level overnight premium is the related night effect. Test long from cash close to next open.
discoveries.source_title: A tug of war: Overnight versus intraday expected returns
discoveries.quote: We document strong overnight and intraday firm-level return continuation along with an offsetting cross-period reversal effect
discoveries.reported_effect: momentum overnight 3-factor alpha 0.95%/month (t=3.65) vs 0.11% intraday - firm level; index transfer REPORTED not documented

discoveries.mechanism: Turn-of-the-month effect: returns from the last trading day through the third trading day of the new month far exceed other days (payroll/pension inflows, month-end institutional cash cycles).
discoveries.source_title: Equity Returns at the Turn of the Month
discoveries.reported_effect: US 1926-2005: 0.15%/day over the 4-day turn vs -0.001% other days; present in 31 of 35 countries

discoveries.mechanism: Dash for cash: the monthly payment cycle forces institutions to raise cash before month-end payment dates, temporarily raising the cost of debt and equity capital (prices pressured), then reverting after.
discoveries.source_title: Dash for Cash: Monthly Market Impact of Institutional Liquidity Needs
discoveries.reported_effect: systematic month-end patterns in liquid markets globally; mutual funds suffer liquidity-related trading

discoveries.mechanism: Halloween / Sell-in-May: Nov-Apr index returns far exceed May-Oct (near zero). calendar_month takes one active_month; sweep active_month over 11,12,1,2,3,4 as one declared family of 6 cells (count as 6 trials).
discoveries.source_title: The Halloween Indicator, 'Sell in May and Go Away': Another Puzzle
discoveries.reported_effect: present in 36 of 37 markets 1970-1998; UK evidence back to 1694

discoveries.mechanism: Anticipated, repeated supply shocks: Treasury prices fall in the days before scheduled auctions (dealers' limited risk capacity, slow end-investor capital) and recover shortly after.
discoveries.source_title: Anticipated and Repeated Shocks in Liquid Markets
discoveries.quote: Treasury security prices in the secondary market decrease significantly in the few days leading up to Treasury auctions and recover shortly thereafter
discoveries.reported_effect: issuance cost 9-18bp of auction size (2007)

discoveries.mechanism: Pre-FOMC drift: equities rise in the 24h before scheduled FOMC announcements (not bonds, not other macro releases). NOTE forced_flow.pre_flow trades the 3-bar drift sign, not an unconditional long - the faithful test needs the signed-window gap below.
discoveries.source_title: The Pre-FOMC Announcement Drift
discoveries.quote: the S&P500 index has on average increased 49 basis points in the 24 hours prior to the FOMC announcements.
discoveries.reported_effect: ~80% of annual realized excess US equity return 1994-2011 earned in the pre-FOMC window; stronger when yield curve flat and implied vol high; international indices similar

discoveries.mechanism: Placebo/negative control: Lucca-Moench find NO pre-FOMC drift in Treasuries; a bond cell that 'passes' flags a leaky or overfit harness.
discoveries.source_title: The Pre-FOMC Announcement Drift
discoveries.quote: we find no such effect in U.S. Treasury securities and other fixed income instruments.
discoveries.reported_effect: null expected (use as a harness canary)

discoveries.mechanism: Time-series momentum: sign of own past 12-month excess return, position scaled by ex-ante EWMA volatility; under-reaction then delayed over-reaction; speculators profit at hedgers' expense; best in extreme markets.
discoveries.source_title: Time series momentum
discoveries.quote: A diversified portfolio of time series momentum strategies across all asset classes delivers substantial abnormal returns with little exposure to standard asset pricing factors
discoveries.reported_effect: significant for each of 58 instruments, 1985-2009; partial reversal beyond 12 months

discoveries.mechanism: Century of trend: equal-weighted 1-, 3- and 12-month TSMOM across 59 markets; positive in every decade since 1880 with low correlation to stocks/bonds, and positive in 8 of the 10 largest 60/40 drawdowns (crisis alpha).
discoveries.source_title: A Century of Evidence on Trend-Following Investing
discoveries.quote: we construct an equal-weighted combination of 1-month, 3-month, and 12-month time series momentum strategies for 59 markets
discoveries.reported_effect: positive average returns every decade 1880-2016; performed well in 8 of 10 largest crises

discoveries.mechanism: Momentum turning points: slow (12m) signals miss turns, fast (1m) signals give false alarms; the four slow/fast sign states (Bull, Correction, Bear, Rebound) carry information - both negative predicts negative returns - and an intermediate/dynamic blend that re-weights after Corrections/Rebounds earns positive alpha.
discoveries.source_title: Momentum turning points
discoveries.quote: Intermediate-speed momentum portfolios, formed by blending slow and fast momentum strategies, translate predictive information in market cycles into positive unconditional alpha
discoveries.reported_effect: dynamic slow/fast blend beats static speeds (JFE 2023)

discoveries.mechanism: Cost-effective safe haven: a sleeve whose value is its payoff in equity crashes can raise the book's GEOMETRIC growth even with a small or negative arithmetic mean; judge it by portfolio delta E[log W], never standalone Sharpe. Trend in havens is the CFD-native convex payoff (no options).
discoveries.source_title: Safe Haven: Investing for Financial Storms
discoveries.reported_effect: Spitznagel: 99.5% S&P + 0.5% tail insurance beat 100% S&P over the long history he shows (REPORTED, book)

discoveries.mechanism: Cryptocurrency returns show strong time-series momentum and are forecast by investor-attention proxies (Google searches, Twitter counts); crypto is MT5 universe only as Fusion CFDs.
discoveries.source_title: Risks and Returns of Cryptocurrency
discoveries.reported_effect: strong TSMOM effect; attention predicts returns (RFS 2021)

discoveries.mechanism: Short-term reversal = compensation for liquidity provision; its expected return rises sharply with lagged VIX as constrained intermediaries withdraw. Run as weekly cross-sectional index reversal conditioned on high implied/realised vol (conditioner is a gap if VIX is not on the box).
discoveries.source_title: Evaporating Liquidity
discoveries.quote: the expected return from liquidity provision is strongly time-varying and highly predictable with the VIX index.
discoveries.reported_effect: even industry-portfolio reversal (weak unconditionally) earns high returns and Sharpe when VIX is high (2007-09)

discoveries.mechanism: Contrarian profits are largely cross-autocorrelation: large-cap returns lead small-cap returns, so a 'reversal' book is secretly a lead-lag book. Test US500 -> US2000 at short lags.
discoveries.source_title: When Are Contrarian Profits Due to Stock Market Overreaction?
discoveries.reported_effect: weekly portfolio returns strongly positively autocorrelated via cross-autocorrelations; large stocks lead small

discoveries.mechanism: Chan's canonical cointegrated pair EWA/EWC (Australia vs Canada, both commodity economies) translated to index CFDs; Kalman-filter hedge ratio and Bollinger-style z entry.
discoveries.source_title: Algorithmic Trading: Winning Strategies and Their Rationale
discoveries.reported_effect: book example EWA-EWC Kalman pair: 26.2% annualized, Sharpe 2.4, 2006-2012 (REPORTED, ETF data)

discoveries.mechanism: Commodity-currency pair mean reversion (Chan: FX and futures intermarket spreads are the classic stationary portfolios); test cointegration and trade the spread z-score.
discoveries.source_title: Algorithmic Trading: Winning Strategies and Their Rationale
discoveries.reported_effect: no paper-specific number for this pair

discoveries.mechanism: PRIOR (negative): the 5-minute opening-range breakout (Zarattini-Aziz, QQQ 2016-2023, 24% hit, +0.13R, no spread/slippage, no OOS) reproduces gross on five index CFDs 2015-2026 but is zero-to-negative net of costs. Keep only variants conditioned on 'in-play' days (volume/gap) and charge realistic spread.
discoveries.source_title: The opening-range breakout paper, replicated on five indices: gross reproduced, net zero
discoveries.quote: Net of costs no market is distinguishable from zero and four of five are negative.
discoveries.reported_effect: gross +0.131R on NQ CFD; net ~0 / negative on all five

discoveries.mechanism: Two-state hidden Markov regimes with time-varying parameters capture abrupt, persistent shifts in mean/vol/correlation; allocating on filtered regime probabilities (model predictive control) cuts drawdowns vs static weights.
discoveries.source_title: Regime-based versus static asset allocation: Letting the data speak / Dynamic portfolio optimization across hidden market regimes
discoveries.reported_effect: regime-based allocation adds value over static rebalancing, notably drawdown reduction (JPM 2015 / QF 2018)

discoveries.mechanism: Combine value with momentum: AMP show value and momentum are negatively correlated within and across asset classes, so a 50/50 combination has a much higher Sharpe than either (pair this cell with the momentum cell above in the ensemble, not as a new trial).
discoveries.source_title: Value and Momentum Everywhere
discoveries.reported_effect: negative value-momentum correlation across all classes studied
